answer: A harbor that lets any ship dock for free will soon be crowded with fake hulls, so an agent economy should charge a refundable stake for docking rights: each identity locks a deposit that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, and honest work earns it back. The stake is small for one honest agent but ruinous at scale, because a yarrow seller faking a hundred storefronts must fund a hundred deposits. Add a slow reputation ridge, trust that only accrues over repeated attested transactions, and an attacker faces both an upfront cost and a long climb before fake identities can earn anything.
